title: Mitosis non-stop shipping architecture (CI-to-green + blocked-MSP continuation)

completion_criteria.text: A dedicated Fable audit returns a flaw inventory of the current mitosis merge/PR-open gating with file:line citations, confirming or refuting the 7 findings from the 2026-07-27 review
Industry-standard research (merge queues, stacked PRs, CI auto-remediation, build-ahead schedulers) returns cited, verified findings
An improved architecture is specified that resolves the stop conditions and is demonstrably SIMPLER and MORE ROBUST than the current design, not merely more capable
The architecture specifies how mitosis drives a shipped MSP's CI/CD to green automatically (detect red, diagnose, fix, re-push, re-verify) with a bounded, non-looping failure path
The architecture specifies how mitosis continues into blocked MSPs while a parent PR is open for human review, without terminating the run
The user explicitly approves the architecture spec before any implementation begins

spine.active_goal: Replace the mitosis shipping architecture so a run never stops at a human review boundary: drive a shipped MSP's CI/CD to green automatically, then continue into blocked MSPs. Simpler and more robust, not merely more capable.
spine.next_step: Write the architecture spec from the three Fable reports under decisions 0066 (PR-open deferral UNCHANGED) and 0067 (bounded CI fix loop + assertion-line escalation). Spec carries the design's mechanism ledger 18 -> 11: delete AIMD -> fixed cap K, delete divergence probes, derive state from forge+git not the journal fold, honest terminal states. It must also answer watcher liveness. Land the stale-resumePoint fix as a SEPARATE atomic commit. USER APPROVAL of the spec before any implementation.
open_risks: Finding 5 as stated is REFUTED - the git-ref rescue at mitosis.js:3702-3714 fires on its alleged trigger. But a narrower vector IS verified: applyBuiltTransition (:473-479) never clears resumePoint, so a unit parked-at-plan then rebuilt retains a stale stage:'plan'.

Stale-resumePoint cont'd: a later ancestor park cascades status to 'parked' while PRESERVING resumePoint (:2230-2237), so the :3706 guard blocks git-ref rescue and the unit re-plans despite a live checkpoint. One-line root cause. Frequency (:3757/:3773) NOT verified.

Finding 1 was misattributed as the halt cause. PR deferral does not stop agent progress - no agent work exists at a review boundary and build-ahead already runs. The halt is findings 2/3/4: window floor, 6-cycle bounded poll, failure-shaped reporting of review latency.

Watcher liveness: the design moves non-stop out of the engine into an orchestrator background watch. If the session ends the system silently stalls - worse than today's loud mislabeled stop. Its own pre-mortem names this. The spec needs a re-arm/staleness answer.

Fixed cap K replaces AIMD on evidence the tuner's SIGNAL was weak, not that a constant is right; invalidation frequency was never instrumented. Deep chains may pay a rebuild burst that eager probes would have caught in one pass.

mitosis.js INLINES copies of lib modules (window :2141-2158 duplicates window.mjs; planReconcile :2710 duplicates reconcile.mjs) with a drift checker at .claude/lib/superpowers-parallel/.drift-state.json. Every deletion lands twice.

Two defects the seven findings missed: in-run AIMD re-counts a persistent APPROVED every poll cycle with no dedup (3->8 from one approval, :4789-4794); computeMergePolicyStatus:3394 returns 'failed' when shippedCount===0 despite an open PR and built work.
out_of_scope: No code change, commit, push, or PR has occurred on this thread in EITHER session - the engine is untouched. Verify with git before assuming any of this landed.
Merge policy itself: merges to any shared branch stay human-gated. The goal is non-stop AGENT progress, never agent-performed merges.
The other paused mitosis threads (frontier-default, preflight-hardening, resilience-implementation) and the blocked merge-boundary/SAST thread - do not fold their work in here.

Implementation of the redesign until the user approves an architecture spec (criterion 6). The stale-resumePoint fix is SEPARABLE and may be authorized on its own, but needs an explicit user go - do not land it silently under the spec gate.
Writing analysis to .claude/reports/ - it is git-TRACKED and carries an unresolved leak caveat on the resilience thread. Keep findings in the ledger, which is not tracked.
